name: Authoritarian socialism
summary: A form of socialism in which a seized revolutionary power runs production and imposes economic equality from above, without pluralist politics. The one open source that names it, Plekhanov's critique of 'authoritarian communism', describes it from outside and states no position on the statements, so this profile records no known answers yet.
scope: Only what the one open defining source ties to the name: Plekhanov's 1883 account of 'authoritarian communism', a seized revolutionary power that runs national production through a socialist caste and imposes economic equality from above. The wider strand Wikipedia describes (Soviet-type party states, Bellamy's utopia) is not stated by any source that could be opened and read, so it is left out until one can; the earlier pass's Lenin, Stalin and Mao texts belong to Leninism, Stalinism and Maoism.

notes: The 11 downloaded books (Sandle, Khlevniuk, Courtois, Pipes, Parenti and others) were searched for 'authoritarian socialism', 'authoritarian communism', 'left-wing dictatorship' and 'autocratic socialism': none uses the name, so none is a defining source. Draper uses 'socialism from above' (a Wikipedia redirect), not the label itself. The earlier audit's Lenin, Stalin and Mao texts are the namesakes' for Leninism, Stalinism and Maoism and are not tied here. Draper's essay never uses the label or any redirect of it ('Socialism-from-Above' is not a redirect and no open source equates it), so Draper's pages (saved in the source library, not cited) cannot pass the coatrack check as the sources stand. The only open text found that names an alias is Plekhanov's 1883 mention of 'authoritarian communism' (s1, a critic's passing use). Books naming the label (Lipow 1991; Halm, Economic Systems; Snavely; Young, Socialism since 1889) are lending-only on archive.org and could not be read. The earlier pass's answers rested on Wikipedia and on texts of Leninism, Stalinism and Maoism that no defining source of this ideology ties to it; they are nulled.
